bounds.domain: One canonical note, optional recording, one additional retained reference, one reviewed deletion,0..7 clock/revision values, and one shared Store readiness state. A separate projection has one queued erase or acknowledgement, one stale review and one cancellation. Publication and acknowledgement are distinct; their outcomes include definite CAS conflict and unknown commit/readback.
bounds.ordering: A successful serialized document commit publishes the note erase and its receipt together. An ambiguous encrypted acknowledgement fences every shared handle until quiescent authoritative reopen. Source tests use exact milliseconds; the base model uses three abstract days. Progress applies only while the explicit finite revision budget remains.
bounds.conformance: Mandatory four separate Node/Vitest processes require all87 exact named cases with zero skips:63 existing domain/revision cases,21 serialized Store/file/direct-route cases and3 actual owner/gateway HTTP/runtime-factory cases. Tests cover pre-dispatch abort, cancelled host verification, lost CAS acknowledgement, readback exception/mismatch, shared-handle fencing, already-committed cancellation, cold recovery without write replay, current collection review, the opt-in setting and independent recording proof.
bounds.limits: Finite source-linked policy and store projections, not whole-implementation refinement. Native recording bytes/erase, actual at-rest encryption of the controlled document port, installed Alpha adoption/UI, background cleanup scheduling, physical devices and arbitrary filesystem/power failure are unproved. Native verification is a trusted controlled port. The queued projection has one caller, not arbitrary overlapping generations. Definite CAS conflict does not refresh an out-of-band writer cache; authoritative reopen is required. Source readback mismatch fences exposure; arbitrary hostile external document rewrites and uncooperative ports are outside the projection.

assumptions: Weak fairness of a successful sweep once expiry is due, readable, unshared and within the finite revision budget. Source invokes maintenance at startup or owner reads; no background timer or wall-clock bound is assumed.
